summary: Castle of Riddles is a text-only adventure game released by Acornsoft for the BBC Micro in 1982 and the Acorn Electron in 1984, written by Peter Killworth. It belonged to a series of text adventures by the same author, and it was not reissued by Topologika, so it became unavailable after 1985 when Acorn Computers withdrew from games publishing. Some of its puzzles later appeared in the Topologika version of Philosopher's Quest.
one_line: Castle of Riddles is a 1982 text adventure by Peter Killworth for the BBC Micro, later unavailable after Acorn left games publishing.
key_facts: Castle of Riddles is a text adventure released by Acornsoft for the BBC Micro in 1982.
Castle of Riddles was released for the Acorn Electron home computer in 1984.
The game was written by Peter Killworth.
Castle of Riddles was one of a series of text adventures written for, or ported to, the BBC Micro by Peter Killworth.
Other text adventures in the series included Countdown to Doom and Philosopher's Quest.
The game uses only text, with no graphics.
The player controls the game using a simple 'verb-noun' format, such as 'Go North' or 'Get lamp'.
Unlike Killworth's other Acornsoft adventures, Castle of Riddles was not updated and reissued by Topologika.
Castle of Riddles became unavailable after 1985.
Acorn Computers, parent company of Acornsoft, pulled out of the games publishing market in 1985.
Some of the puzzles from Castle of Riddles were included in the Topologika version of Philosopher's Quest.
